messages:
alex: seeing repeated P95/P99 spikes in shared-gpu-pool in us-west this morning, queue depth hit 180% of our configured soft-limit around 06:02 UTC. some tenants spiked and pushed KV-cache churn, looks like noisy-neighbor pattern.
maya: ugh. any tenancy IDs? can we pin down if it's batching behavior or inference length?
alex: tenant ids T-82 and T-311. payloads are long-gen with many short bursts, they keep getting retried -> higher concurrency. logs show lots of small requests that break batching.
jonathan: two quick suggestions: 1) apply a temporary per-tenant recovery window that reduces concurrent inflight to 1-2 for offenders, 2) enable short prefix cache TTL for those tenants to avoid KV churn. both are soft actions (no hard evict).
maya: +1 for recovery window. can we do automatic backoff instead of manual ops? maybe a sliding window that increases penalty with repeated violations.
ci-bot: deploy pipeline started for branch "infra/noisy-tenant-recovery" (build #8142). status: running tests.
sre_oncall: we need to be careful with automatic backoff — hitting enterprise customers with sudden rate drops will cause ticket storms. propose a 5-min canary window and SMS paging only if tail > 10s after mitigation.
leah: agree with canary. also we should surface a clear reason in tenant metrics so SRE/support can explain: add a "mitigation_reason" label on the tenant dashboard.
jonathan: implementation sketch: add a tenant_score that accumulates from excess queue_time + retries + cache_misses. when score > threshold -> enter Recovery state: limits = {concurrency: max(2, floor(weight*0.1)), token_rate: 50%}. Score decays exponentially with half-life 20m.
maya: love the score idea. can we also tie to billing alerts? noisy behavior increases cost — optionally alert tenant billing contact. opt-in flag for automated billing notifications.
alex: quick config snippet for the recovery window we tested locally:
```
recovery_policy:
  window: 300 # seconds
  concurrency_limit: 2
  score_threshold: 120
  decay_half_life: 1200 # seconds
```
jonathan: runtime changes needed: admission controller hook plus a small state store (redis) per region to accumulate scores. should be cheap. Also route mitigation decision to local region to avoid cross-region latency.
sre_oncall: ops checklist for rollout:
- 5% of clusters in us-west as canary
- 5-min canary window with notifications to #incidents
- rollback on any increase in overall error rate or customer complaints
leah: can we add a "soft-grace" phase where we prefer request shaping (drop batch size to 1, add jitter) before lowering rate? that gives customers a chance to adapt without immediate QoS hit.
maya: yep, sequence: shape -> rate-limit -> recovery-window -> human-review. Also capture sample requests for root-cause analysis (PII-scrubbed).
alex: CI green. rolling canary starting now for 5% us-west nodes. watch dashboards: shared-pool/queue_depth, tenant/T-82/score, overall_p99. paging rule temporarily relaxed to only > 12s.
ci-bot: deploy #8142 succeeded to canary group.
sre_oncall: early telemetry: queue_depth down ~40% at 06:20 UTC, T-82 score climbed then decayed after 7 minutes. no customer page yet.
leah: good sign. let's keep the canary for 2 hours and then expand to 20% if stable. add runbook snippet to support team.
maya: will draft support blurb and add opt-in billing notice.
jonathan: afterwards we should run a simulation: synthetic noisy tenants with varied retry strategies to tune score thresholds. I can spin up a harness.
alex: thanks all — if anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:
